name: Collective Rights Management Directive
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission application report based mainly on stakeholder views, with two supporting studies
summary: The Commission's 2021 report found the Directive had a positive effect on rightholders and on licensing, including multi-territorial licensing of music online, and saw no need to revise it; stakeholders still reported problems with user reporting and timely distribution of royalties. The assessment rests on consultation and two commissioned studies, not on measured outcomes.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Report on the application of Directive 2014/26/EU on collective management of copyright and related rights and multi-territorial licensing of rights in musical works for online use, SWD(2021) 338
literature.title: Report on the application of Directive 2014/26/EU on collective management of copyright and related rights and multi-territorial licensing of rights in musical works for online use
literature.method: application report (stakeholder consultation, two external studies)
literature.outcomes: governance and transparency of collecting societies; licensing
literature.headline: Positive effect on rightholders and the licensing market; no need for review; remaining problems with users' reporting and timely distribution of royalties
literature.summary_plain: The Commission concluded the rules on collecting societies were working and did not need changes, though some payment and reporting problems persisted.
literature.quality: Commission self-assessment based on stakeholder views
